summary: Only a Kohen who can do the avodah that day gets a share of the korbanos' meat and skins. A Kohen with a blemish gets a share but may not offer, and a Kohen who was tamei when the blood was thrown gets no share.

chunks.en: One who toveled today and one who still has to bring his korban for kapparah
chunks.st: A priest who was ritually impure who immersed that day and is waiting for nightfall for the purification process to be completed, and a priest who has not yet brought an atonement
chunks.stMore: offering to complete the purification process, e.g., a zav and a leper who did not bring their requisite atonement offerings, who are not yet permitted to partake of sacrificial meat,

chunks.en: do not get a share of the korbanos to eat at night.
chunks.st: do not receive a share of sacrificial meat along with the other members of the patrilineal priestly family serving in the Temple that day, in order to partake of it in the evening
chunks.stMore: after the offerings were sacrificed, even though after nightfall he would be permitted to partake of the offerings.

chunks.en: A mourner may touch, but does not offer,
chunks.st: A priest who is an acute mourner, i.e., if one of his relatives for whom he is obligated to mourn died that day, is permitted to touch sacrificial meat, as he is not ritually impure. But he may not sacrifice offerings,

chunks.en: and does not get a share to eat at night.
chunks.st: and he does not receive a share of sacrificial meat in order to partake of it in the evening.

summary: If the mizbeach did not get the meat of an olah, the Kohanim do not get its skin. But an olah shechted for the wrong purpose, or a woman's olah, still gives its skin to the Kohanim.

chunks.en: Any olah whose meat the mizbeach did not get,
chunks.st: In the case of any burnt offering for which the altar did not acquire its flesh,
chunks.stMore: e.g., if it was disqualified prior to the sprinkling of its blood,

chunks.en: the Kohanim do not get its skin,
chunks.st: the priests did not acquire its hide,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to the burnt offering:

words.note: In the same place in the Torah.

chunks.en: "a man's olah,"
chunks.st: “And the priest that sacrifices a man’s burnt offering,
chunks.stMore: the priest shall have to himself the hide of the burnt offering that he has sacrificed” (Leviticus 7:8),

chunks.en: an olah that counted for a man.
chunks.st: indicating that the priest acquires only the hide of a burnt offering that satisfied the obligation of a man. Nevertheless,

chunks.en: An olah that was shechted for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: in a case of a burnt offering that was slaughtered not for its sake but for the sake of another offering,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא עָלְתָה לַבְּעָלִים,
chunks.en: even though it did not count for the owner,
chunks.st: although it did not satisfy the obligation of the owner,

chunks.en: its skin goes to the Kohanim.
chunks.st: its hide goes to the priests. In addition, although the verse states:

chunks.he: אֶחָד עוֹלַת הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד עוֹלַת הָאִשָּׁה,
chunks.en: Both a man's olah and a woman's olah,
chunks.st: “A man’s burnt offering,” in the case of both the burnt offering of a man and the burnt offering of a woman,

chunks.en: their skins go to the Kohanim.
chunks.st: their hides go to the priests.

summary: The skins of less holy korbanos belong to the owners, and the skins of the holiest korbanos belong to the Kohanim. This is learned from the olah: if the Kohanim get its skin though they do not eat its meat, they surely get the skins of korbanos they do eat.

chunks.en: The skins of less holy korbanos go to the owners,
chunks.st: The hides of offerings of lesser sanctity belong to the owners;

chunks.en: and the skins of the holiest korbanos go to the Kohanim.
chunks.st: the hides of offerings of the most sacred order belong to the priests.

chunks.st: an a fortiori inference:

chunks.st: If for a burnt offering, for which

chunks.en: whose meat they do not get,

chunks.en: then the holiest korbanos,

chunks.st: the priests acquire its flesh,

chunks.en: is it not right that they should get its skin?
chunks.st: is it not right that they should acquire its hide?

summary: If a korban became pasul before it was skinned, the Kohanim do not get its skin. Rabbi Chanina never saw a skin being burned, and Rabbi Akiva learned from this that a bechor found to be a treifah still gives its skin, but the Sages disagree.

chunks.en: All korbanos that had
chunks.st: If any offerings

chunks.en: something make them pasul before they were skinned,
chunks.st: of the most sacred order were disqualified prior to their flaying,

chunks.en: their skins do not go to the Kohanim.
chunks.st: their hides do not go to the priests;
chunks.stMore: rather, they are burned together with the flesh in the place of burning.

chunks.en: After they were skinned,
chunks.st: If they were disqualified after their flaying,

chunks.en: their skins go to the Kohanim.
chunks.st: their hides go to the priests.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina, the assistant of the Kohanim, said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina, the deputy High Priest, said:

chunks.en: In all my days I never saw a skin
chunks.st: In all my days, I never saw a hide

chunks.en: going out to the place of burning.
chunks.st: going out to the place of burning.

chunks.st: From the statement of Rabbi Ḥanina, the deputy High Priest, we learned that

chunks.en: that if one skins a bechor and it is found to be a treifah,
chunks.st: in a case where one flays the firstborn offering, and the animal is later discovered to have a wound that would have caused it to die within twelve months [tereifa],

chunks.en: the Kohanim may still use its skin.
chunks.st: the halakha is that the priests may derive benefit [sheye’otu] from its hide.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,

chunks.en: rather, it goes out to the place of burning.
chunks.st: rather, if after flaying it is discovered that the animal was unfit before it was flayed, the hide goes out to the place of burning.

summary: The bulls and goats that are burned, when burned the right way, are burned outside Yerushalayim and make the clothes of those who burn them tamei. If they became pasul, they are burned in the Beis HaMikdash and do not make clothes tamei.

chunks.en: The bulls that are burned and the goats that are burned,
chunks.st: With regard to bulls that are burned, i.e., the bull of Yom Kippur, the bull of the anointed priest, and the bull brought for an unwitting communal sin, which are burned after their blood is sprinkled and their sacrificial portions burned on the altar, and goats that are burned,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the goat of Yom Kippur and the goat brought for the unwitting communal transgression of the prohibition against idol worship,

chunks.en: when they are burned the way of their mitzvah,
chunks.st: when they are burned in accordance with their mitzva,

chunks.en: are burned in the place of the ashes and make clothes tamei.
chunks.st: they are burned in the place of the ashes (see Leviticus 4:12) outside of Jerusalem, and they render the garments of the priests who tend to their burning impure (see Leviticus 4:25).

chunks.en: But if they are not burned the way of their mitzvah,
chunks.st: And if these offerings are not burned in accordance with their mitzva
chunks.stMore: because they were disqualified, and offerings that are disqualified are also burned,

chunks.he: נִשְׂרָפִין בְּבֵית הַבִּירָה וְאֵינָם מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים:
chunks.en: they are burned in the Birah and do not make clothes tamei.
chunks.st: they are burned in the place of burning in the bira, and they do not render the garments of the priests who tend to their burning impure.

words.note: A name for the Beis HaMikdash.

summary: The Kohanim carried the bulls and goats that are burned on poles. The ones who left the courtyard first made their clothes tamei first. Rabbi Shimon says the clothes become tamei only once the fire has caught most of the meat.

chunks.en: They would carry them on poles.
chunks.st: The priests would carry the bulls and the goats that are burned suspended on poles.

chunks.en: If the first ones went outside the wall
chunks.st: When the first priests, carrying the front of the pole, emerged outside the wall of the

chunks.en: of the courtyard and the last ones did not go out,
chunks.st: Temple courtyard and the latter priests did not yet emerge,

chunks.en: the first ones make their clothes tamei,
chunks.st: the first priests render their garments impure,

chunks.en: and the last ones do not make their clothes tamei
chunks.st: and the latter priests do not render their garments impure

chunks.en: until they go out.
chunks.st: until they emerge.

chunks.en: If both these and those went out,
chunks.st: When both these and those priests emerged,

chunks.en: both these and those make their clothes tamei.
chunks.st: they render their garments impure.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: both these and those do not make their clothes tamei
chunks.st: They do not render their garments impure,
chunks.stMore: as this halakha applies only to those who burn the offerings.

chunks.en: until the fire catches most of them.
chunks.st: And even then their garments do not become ritually impure until the fire is ignited in the majority of the offerings.

chunks.en: Once the meat is burned through,
chunks.st: Once the flesh is completely scorched, with no moisture remaining,

chunks.en: the one who burns it does not make his clothes tamei.
chunks.st: one who then burns the remains does not render his garments impure.
